tests.title: Unit 2: Planning and Decision Making – Practice Test 1

options: Deciding in advance what to do, how to do it, when to do it and who will do it
questions.explanation: It bridges the gap between where we are and where we want to go.

options: Deciding in advance what to do, how to do it, when to do it and who is to do it
questions.explanation: It bridges the gap from where we are to where we want to go.

questions.question_text: A feature of planning is that it is:
questions.explanation: It involves choice among alternatives.

questions.question_text: Planning is called the primary function of management because:
options: It precedes all other functions, which depend on plans
questions.explanation: Organising, staffing, directing and controlling follow plans.

questions.question_text: Planning is a pervasive function because it:
options: Is done by top management only
Is required at all levels and in all departments
questions.explanation: Every manager plans.

questions.question_text: Planning is a continuous process because:
options: Plans are revised as conditions change
questions.explanation: There is a plan for each period.

options: It looks ahead and anticipates future conditions
It looks only at the past
questions.explanation: It is based on forecasts.

options: Providing direction, reducing uncertainty and facilitating control
questions.explanation: Plans give a framework for action.

options: Anticipating changes and preparing for them
questions.explanation: Forecasting helps managers get ready.

options: Providing standards against which actual performance is compared
questions.explanation: There is no control without plans.

questions.question_text: Planning and controlling are called "inseparable twins" because:
options: Planning sets the standards and controlling checks performance against them
questions.explanation: Each depends on the other.

questions.question_text: A limitation of planning is that it:
options: Leads to rigidity and may not work in a dynamic environment
questions.explanation: It is also time-consuming and costly.

options: Managers may stick to the plan even when circumstances change
questions.explanation: Employees may follow plans blindly.

questions.question_text: Planning does not work well in a dynamic environment because:
options: Changes may make plans out of date quickly
questions.explanation: It becomes difficult to forecast.

questions.question_text: Limitations of planning can be overcome by:
options: Making plans flexible, reviewing them regularly and involving staff
questions.explanation: Contingency plans help.

questions.question_text: Planning differs from forecasting in that forecasting:
options: Predicts future conditions, while planning decides what to do about them
questions.explanation: Forecasts are a premise for plans.

questions.question_text: Planning differs from budgeting in that a budget:
options: Is a numerical statement of expected results and a type of plan, whereas planning is broader
questions.explanation: Budgets express plans in numbers.

options: Mission, objectives, strategies, policies, procedures, rules, programmes and budgets
questions.explanation: They form a hierarchy.

options: The basic purpose or reason for the existence of an organisation
questions.explanation: It answers "why do we exist?".

options: Specific, Measurable, Achievable, Relevant and Time-bound
questions.explanation: They are clear targets with a deadline.

options: A comprehensive plan to achieve long-term objectives considering the environment and competition
questions.explanation: It decides the direction of the organisation.

questions.question_text: The components of a strategy include:
options: Environmental scanning, resource allocation and competitive positioning
questions.explanation: It also involves a choice of businesses.

options: A general guideline for decision making, e.g., a promotion or pricing policy
questions.explanation: It gives the framework for decisions.

options: A chronological sequence of steps to carry out a task, e.g., a purchase procedure
questions.explanation: It specifies how work is done.

options: The way in which a single step of a procedure is performed
questions.explanation: It is more detailed than a procedure.

tests.title: Unit 2: Planning and Decision Making – Practice Test 2

options: A specific, definite statement of what to do or not to do, with no discretion, e.g., "No smoking"
questions.explanation: It must be followed strictly.

options: A comprehensive plan that includes objectives, policies, procedures and resources for a set of activities
questions.explanation: E.g., a plan for launching a new product.

options: A single-use plan with a specific objective and fixed time, e.g., constructing a plant
questions.explanation: It is part of a programme.

options: A statement of expected results expressed in numerical terms
questions.explanation: It is a financial or quantitative plan.

questions.question_text: A policy differs from a procedure and a rule in that a policy is:
options: A flexible guide for thinking, a procedure is a series of steps, and a rule is a rigid directive
questions.explanation: Rules allow no discretion.

questions.question_text: Policy differs from procedure in that policy:
options: Guides decisions, while procedure guides actions in sequence
questions.explanation: Policy is general; procedure is specific.

questions.question_text: Policy differs from strategy in that a policy is:
options: A guide for decisions within limits, while a strategy is a plan to deal with competition and the environment
questions.explanation: Strategy is about direction and positioning.

questions.question_text: Strategic plans are made by _____, tactical plans by _____, and operational plans by _____:
options: Top management; middle management; lower management
questions.explanation: They differ in time frame and scope.

questions.question_text: Single-use plans differ from standing plans in that single-use plans:
options: Are made for one occasion, e.g., a project, whereas standing plans are used repeatedly, e.g., policies
questions.explanation: Standing plans: policies, procedures, rules.

options: A backup plan to be used if the original plan fails or conditions change
questions.explanation: It prepares the firm for uncertain events.

questions.question_text: The first step in the planning process is:
questions.explanation: Everything else is guided by objectives.

questions.question_text: Setting objectives is the first step because:
options: It gives direction to all further steps
questions.explanation: Plans are designed to achieve objectives.

options: An assumption about the future environment in which the plan will operate
questions.explanation: It forms the base of the plan.

options: Internal and external, tangible and intangible, controllable and uncontrollable
questions.explanation: They help make forecasts consistent.

questions.question_text: Internal premises relate to _____, and external premises relate to _____:
options: The organisation (e.g., policies, resources); the environment (e.g., economy, laws)
questions.explanation: The firm can control internal premises.

questions.question_text: Tangible premises can be _____, and intangible premises _____:
options: Measured in numbers (e.g., costs); are hard to measure (e.g., morale)
questions.explanation: Both affect planning.

options: The organisation can influence, while uncontrollable ones, like government policy, it cannot
questions.explanation: Managers focus on those they can influence.

questions.question_text: Planning premises are the foundation of planning because:
options: Plans are based on assumptions about the future
questions.explanation: Wrong premises give wrong plans.

options: Trend analysis, regression, expert opinion (Delphi) and market surveys
questions.explanation: They predict future values.

options: A forecasting method using anonymous, repeated rounds of expert opinion until consensus
questions.explanation: Experts do not meet face to face.
Internal strengths/weaknesses and external opportunities/threats.

Political, Economic, Social, Technological, Legal and Environmental factors
Profit, equity, stock, tax, loans, earnings
Product, entry, sales, trade, labour, economy
questions.explanation: It scans the external macro environment.

options: Stars, cash cows, question marks and dogs
questions.explanation: Based on market growth and relative market share.

options: Threat of new entrants, bargaining power of buyers and suppliers, threat of substitutes and rivalry
questions.explanation: It analyses industry competition.

questions.question_text: A characteristic of a good policy is that it is:
options: Clear, consistent, flexible and in line with objectives
questions.explanation: It should also be stable and understood.

tests.title: Unit 2: Planning and Decision Making – Practice Test 3

options: Originated, appealed, imposed and implied; or general and departmental
questions.explanation: They differ by their source.

options: Policies for functional areas such as marketing, finance and HR (e.g., credit policy)
questions.explanation: They guide each function.

questions.question_text: A purchase procedure typically begins with:
options: Requisition, then inviting quotations, order placement, receipt and payment
questions.explanation: Each step is in sequence.

options: Identifying vacancies, advertising, screening, tests and interviews, and selection
questions.explanation: It leads to selection and placement.

questions.question_text: Policies and procedures are needed to:
options: Ensure consistency and save time in decision making
questions.explanation: They guide uniform action.

options: Choosing the best alternative from the available alternatives
questions.explanation: It is at the heart of management.

questions.question_text: Herbert Simon said that decision making:
questions.explanation: "Management is decision making."

questions.question_text: A characteristic of decision making is that it:
options: Involves a choice among alternatives and a commitment to action
questions.explanation: It is a goal-directed process.

options: It determines the success of every function
questions.explanation: Every plan involves decisions.

options: Routine, repetitive decisions made by rules and procedures, e.g., reordering stock
questions.explanation: Lower levels handle many.

options: Unique, non-routine decisions with no set procedure, e.g., launching a new business
questions.explanation: Top managers handle them.

questions.question_text: Programmed decisions differ from non-programmed decisions in that programmed decisions are:
options: Routine and structured, while non-programmed are novel and unstructured
questions.explanation: They differ in nature and level.

questions.question_text: Strategic decisions are made by _____, tactical by _____, operational by _____:
questions.explanation: They differ in scope and time horizon.

options: Made by a group of people, as opposed to individual decisions made by one person
questions.explanation: They are slower but better informed.

options: Major, one-time decisions involving large investment, while routine decisions are repetitive
questions.explanation: E.g., location of a plant.

questions.question_text: Organisational decisions are made in the capacity of:
options: A manager and can be delegated, while personal decisions concern the manager as an individual
questions.explanation: Personal decisions cannot be delegated.
They differ in knowledge of outcomes.

questions.question_text: Simon's three phases of decision making are:
questions.explanation: Intelligence finds problems; design develops alternatives; choice selects.

questions.question_text: The rational decision-making process begins with:
questions.explanation: Then collect information, develop alternatives, evaluate and choose.

questions.question_text: The rational model assumes that the decision maker:
options: Has complete information and chooses the best alternative to maximise results
questions.explanation: It is an ideal model.

options: Decision makers have limited information and ability, so they "satisfice" by choosing an acceptable solution
questions.explanation: Satisficing means choosing the first satisfactory option.

questions.question_text: The four decision-making styles of Rowe and Mason are:
questions.explanation: They differ in tolerance for ambiguity and focus.

options: Fast and focused on results with low tolerance of ambiguity
questions.explanation: Decisions are made quickly with little information.

options: Careful and data-driven with a high tolerance for ambiguity
questions.explanation: They want complete information.

options: Creative and long-term, with many options considered
questions.explanation: They are idea-oriented.

tests.title: Unit 2: Planning and Decision Making – Practice Test 4

options: People-oriented, concerned with the acceptance of the decision by others
questions.explanation: They prefer consensus and teamwork.

options: Involves subordinates in the decision process
Is made by the manager alone
questions.explanation: It increases commitment.

questions.question_text: An advantage of group decision making is:
options: More information and diverse views, with greater acceptance
questions.explanation: Group decisions often improve quality.

questions.question_text: A disadvantage of group decision making is that it:
options: Takes more time and may suffer from groupthink
questions.explanation: It also may be dominated by a few members.

options: A tendency of group members to seek agreement and ignore alternatives
questions.explanation: It suppresses dissent.

options: A technique to generate many ideas without criticism
questions.explanation: Evaluation comes later.

options: Has members write ideas independently, then discuss and rank them by voting
questions.explanation: It reduces domination by a few.

options: A diagram showing decision alternatives, chance events and outcomes to compare expected values
questions.explanation: It helps in decisions under risk.

questions.question_text: Payoffs of 50,000, 20,000 and −10,000 with probabilities 0.3, 0.5, 0.2. The EMV is:
Option A: 60% chance of Rs 1,00,000 and 40% chance of Rs 20,000; Option B: certain Rs 70,000. The better option is:
options: Option A, since EMV is Rs 80,000
Option B, since EMV of A is Rs 68,000

questions.question_text: Plans A, B, C have payoffs (40, 10), (30, 20) and (25, 25). The maximin choice is:
questions.explanation: The minimum payoffs are 10, 20 and 25; the best minimum is 25.

questions.question_text: For the same plans, the maximax choice is:
questions.explanation: The maximum payoffs are 40, 30 and 25.

questions.question_text: The minimax regret criterion chooses the alternative that:
questions.explanation: Regret is the difference from the best outcome in each state.

options: Relying on biases and heuristics instead of analysis
questions.explanation: Bias distorts judgment.

options: Mental shortcuts or rules of thumb used in decision making
questions.explanation: They save time but may cause bias.

options: Giving too much weight to the first information received, e.g., a first price offered
questions.explanation: Later judgments stay close to the anchor.

options: Seeking information that supports one's existing beliefs and ignoring contradicting evidence
questions.explanation: It limits open evaluation.

options: Judging likelihood by how easily examples come to mind
questions.explanation: Vivid or recent events seem more likely.

options: Overestimating one's own knowledge or ability to predict
questions.explanation: It leads to excessive risk.

options: Believing after an event that one "knew it all along"
questions.explanation: It distorts learning from outcomes.

options: Reaching different decisions depending on how the same information is presented
questions.explanation: E.g., 90% survival vs 10% mortality.

options: Continuing with a decision because of past investment that cannot be recovered
questions.explanation: Only future costs and benefits matter.

options: Increasing commitment to a failing course of action despite negative evidence
questions.explanation: It is related to the sunk cost fallacy.

options: Crediting successes to oneself and blaming failures on external factors
questions.explanation: It distorts evaluation of performance.

questions.question_text: Managers can reduce decision biases by:
options: Seeking diverse views, using data, and having structured decision processes
questions.explanation: Devil's advocate and checklists also help.
